Voice Labels Case

A desk console for the Raspberry Pi label printer. The 7" screen reclines 20° above a sloped deck holding the TALK and PRINT buttons. A closed power pod behind the base holds the USB power brick and a switched, fused mains socket. The housing and pod join the base with sliding dovetails; tick Spread apart to see how they come off. Drag to turn the model, scroll or pinch to zoom.

How it joins

Housing to baseTwo dovetail rails under the housing slide down the seat into slots in the base
Pod to baseDrops onto two vertical dovetail rails on the back of the base
LocksFour quarter-turn lock pins, two per part, through the side walls and across grooves in the rails. Turn a pin's wing head upright to unlock it and pull it out

How the pins lock

Close-up of one pin and a piece of the wall, shown see-through so you can watch the lug behind it. Drag to turn.
Loading…
  1. Hold the pin with its wing head upright, lined up with the slot at the top of the hole, and push it in. The lug on the shaft passes through the slot.
  2. Turn the head a quarter turn, either way. Behind the wall the lug rides up a small ramp, pulling the head tight against the wall.
  3. At 90° the lug drops into a notch with a click. Locked: it can't pull out, and it can't turn back by itself. A stop just past the notch stops it going too far.
  4. To unlock, twist the head back to upright. It takes a firm twist to get the lug back over the ramp.
  5. Pull the pin out.

The same lock is on all eight pins: two hold the housing on the base, two hold the pod, and four hold the screen in the housing. Head crosswise means locked.
